method.title: How these figures are measured
method.successRate: Backup success rate: succeeded runs divided by succeeded and failed runs that finished in the period. Cancelled runs were stopped on purpose and are not counted.
method.volume: Protected data is the newest backup of every protected object. Stored bytes are the encrypted, deduplicated pack files; packs removed by garbage collection no longer appear in earlier intervals.
method.dedup: Deduplication ratio: all retained backups added up, divided by the bytes stored.
method.readiness: Proven restorable: objects whose newest backup was rated “Ready” or “Attention” by a restore check of that very backup. A backup taken after the last check stays unproven until it is checked itself; objects never checked or never backed up are not proven, and damage the storage check finds after a check counts as not restorable.
method.status: Excluded objects are not protected and objects removed from their source count while they still have a backup. Only an object's current status is stored, so an object excluded today is left out of earlier intervals too.
method.throttling: Throttling waits are what Microsoft Graph imposed on finished jobs; {appName} waits as long as Microsoft asks instead of retrying sooner.
